title: hotline miami
text: There's absolutely nothing I can respect more than a game that knows what it wants to be, and Hotline Miami knows EXACTLY what it wants to be: fast paced violence! With tightly grouped rooms and corridors, this games level design allows for quick impulsive action to be the one true tactic. When I had first played this game, I was super cautious, and was pretty much up to the epilogue until finally I just snapped (after dying for the 10 billionth time regardless of careful planning of the enemies behavior,) and just slammed through doors, rapidly pressing the fire key, slashing everyone and everything I passed by, and found that was actually making further progress. “Surely, this is just a fluke! Pure luck, added with strange level design!” I thought, but when I just simply let loose and mindlessly blasted through every level, I found it was the most effective way to play. Enemy AI is intentionally unreliable: changing patterns, braking rules that you find aren't so concrete, as they suddenly brake from their routine patrols, combined with varying reaction times from a wizened martial arts master to a handicapped rock. Add this to the fact that the respawn is instantaneous once you press the respawn key (matching the mood of when your just madly slamming away at the buttons going “woiehfpuhqwerp;oghbeipoqurhgvhdfgpovghjqpoerihjf;lbsdhg” because you died AGAIN) it is a game that punishes you for being slow and calculated, even literally, as waiting too long in an area will actually give you a lower score, whereas running into a room full of enemies and impulsively breaking each of their skulls in will reward you for your “boldness” at the end of the level, resulting in a higher score. It is a game that wants you to act like the mood it's trying to convey: impulsive, senseless, fast paced violence. The only real “planning” aspect of the game is choosing from one of the many masks at the very beginning of the level, which will give you different abilities throughout the level, some to add more ease, and even some to add more challenge (there's one that only lets you see a few inches in front of you.) And these masks are ♥♥♥♥ing fun to play around with! My all-time favorite is one that you get for completing the game that lets you run SUPER fast, even further adding to fast pace of the gameplay. Other than these masks, the only best bet you have is twitch reaction impulse, and hopes that the enemy won't be even more hair-trigger than you are. The art style also really puts you in the mood, as psychedelic mixes of invasive neon colors (namely red) fill the screen with pixel art that I feel does a good job of putting you into the time period, and it all gives this feeling of “These characters are quite clearly on drugs.” I know that to some, the whole pixel look is a bit of a turn-off, but trust me, I feel like with the setting of this game, it actually really works, and I've never been confused as to what I was looking at, so It's all clear enough to understand what's going on. And the color scheme is extremely refreshing to me, with so many games, some not even being as violent and dark as this, seem to have ugly, bland color palettes, whereas this one seems to put in extremely vibrant colors, probably to even further excite you as you play through. So with all this talk of violence, blood, flashing bright colors, and impulse, you may be thinking this game is probably for the unintelligent spaz that you can easily find playing Call of Duty, drinking Mountain Dew with their Ritalin, and while I can certainly see those kinds of people playing this game, skipping through cutscenes just to get to the next level to kill more people, if you actually look through those cutscenes and listen to what's being said, this game actually has what I feel is a pretty fitting message: violence is pointless! “Whaaaat?” I hear you cry, “But you were just talking about how violent this game is, and how fun it is to partake in that violence!” Yes, but the game actually has a voice of reason in there that actually mocks you throughout the whole game. You don't play as a good guy, and it makes that known. The guy that you play as is doing things without even knowing or caring to know why, and it kind of makes fun of him for that, pointing out that all of this violence and killing can't be justified (okay, sure, I suppose the people you kill in it are also pretty bad, but I think that's more of just because this takes place in a world of bad people killing bad people.) I will admit: the message is pretty minimal in this game, and if you want to get more into it, you'd have to look at the second game, but trust me, this game actually does point out that there's no point or justification for what you do. With a solid soundtrack, aesthetic, game-style, and level design, added with some decent writing to boot, I'd say that this game is a must have! Also, before I forget: DO NOT GET THIS GAME IF YOU DON'T HAVE A CONTROLLER! Trust me, this is a great game, and I HIGHLY recommend it, but the controls with just a mouse and keyboard are beyond horrible, they're Donald Trump. Once you get a controller, it should be smooth sailing from there.

text: I have played Hotline Miami for 39 hours and have 100% on the game. Ive have never in my gaming life 100% a game because it just didn't appeal to me, the games never offered me anything in return for 100%ing the it. However Hotline Miami did, not by giving me a item in game or any sort of unlockable but answers to the questions i was asking myself while playing the game. When I found every puzzle piece and got one answer to my many questions i went ahead and got an A+ on every level becasue maybe just maybe the game will give me more answers. I have never played a game with such a well built game world that had me actively searching for game lore. But what is Hotline Miami? Hotline Miami is a fast-paced, bloody mayhem, murder simulator as i like to call it where you start each level by choosing a mask to wear that will give a slight advantage that will help you and then you walk into the building and either shoot, stab, or smash every living thing in sight. The game promotes and even rewards killing your enemies in the most violent way for example you get lets say 100 points for just shooting some one but 1000 or so for smashing them in the face with a door then sticking a brick in their mouths and stomping on it. More points equals more weapons and more weapons means more ways to earn points which in turn leads to more weapons which goes on until you unlock all weapons. Now what is the story of Hotline Miami? Well the game has a very odd and unique way of story telling but you the player are receiving strange phone calls urging you to kill everyone in a certain place so of course you go and do it, from here the plot thickens however i cant go much further then this due to spoilers, and I highly recomend you stay from spoilers of this game, ruins the whole thing. Now one last thing I want to mention is that this game has an amazing soundtrack and deserves more credit then it gets for its soundtrack. I would highley recomend this game to anyone with the stomach to handle it. Everything about this game is good the only complaint I have is that it sometimes just crashes to desktop but that may be a thing with windows 8 so I cant really blame the game. 10/10 Mastapeice "Do you like hurting people?"

text: Poorly ported console game. No Video options, Locked to 4:3 aspect ratio, No resolution settings, Locked at 60 fps. The game does not like being alt+tabbed. Friendly fire means that a Ranged + Melee multiplayer setup results in the ranged character shooting the melee character more often than not.
